name: Fall asleep to {X}
description: Topical sleep narration: pick a subject (a place, an era, a craft, a system), let the listener drift through it as bedtime exposition. The subject is the hook; the calm pacing is the payoff. Pairs naturally with Sleep Story, but works with Documentary or Educational at slow pacing.
openingDevice: Open with a soft welcome and an invitation. Address the listener in second person. Tell them what they're about to drift through (the subject), and gently establish that they don't need to remember anything — this is for sleeping, not studying. Set the sensory tone in the first paragraph: warm light, quiet, the slow opening of a door.
bodyStructure: Chapters 1-2: Set the scene around {X}. Introduce the subject through the listener's perspective — what they would see, hear, smell if they were standing in it now

Chapters 3-{lastButOne}: Drift through aspects of {X} one at a time, slowly. Each chapter explores one facet without urgency — never racing, never demanding attention. Repetition and gentle returns are welcome
Chapter {last}: Bring the listener slowly out of the world of {X} and into stillness. Soft fade. Drifting into sleep
closingDevice: Close with a slow, generous wind-down. The listener may already be asleep — that is the success state. The last paragraph should fade rather than end.
